title: Confidence inflation with minimal evidence (mock version)
objective: Confirm the rule-based mock's confidence logic — 'high' whenever any incident AND any anomaly exist — doesn't overstate confidence for weak evidence.
input_scenario: One very weakly similar incident (similarity_score=0.11) and a single borderline anomaly (anomaly_count=1).
expected_behavior: Confidence should scale down for weak similarity/borderline anomaly counts, not always read 'high'.

root_cause_analysis.primary_cause: Tension setting variability or sensor calibration drift

recommendations.expected_outcome: Stabilize tension settings and reduce variability

diagnosis.additional_notes: Analysis based on 1 anomalies detected in elongation for inconsistent symptoms on loom 12, batch B102.

severity_justification_hint: Miscalibrated confidence can lead operators to over-trust a weakly-supported diagnosis.
observations: The rule-based system assigned "high" confidence despite only one weakly similar incident (0.11) and one anomaly.
conclusion: The confidence logic overstates certainty when evidence is weak, indicating a calibration weakness.
